newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Paipote smelter votes Thurs on pay offer.
newsitem.headline: Chile Paipote smelter votes Thurs on pay offer.

text.p: Workers at Chilean state mining company Enami's Paipote smelter will vote Thursday on whether to accept the company's final pay offer in collective wage talks, said an Enami spokesman.
The vote will end at around 2200 local (0100 GMT Friday) with the result known several hours later, spokesman Guillermo Hormazabal told Reuters.
Officials from Empresa Nacional de Mineria (Enami) handed details of the offer to union leaders on Monday, he said.
Enami is optimistic that workers at the smelter, which produces 68,000 tonnes of copper anodes a year, will accept the deal to replace the existing contract which expires month-end, he said.
"We are always optimistic that we will reach an agreement," said Hormazabal.
He declined to give details of the offer. Union officials have said Enami is offering a five year contract to replace the current two year pact.
Workers at Paipote went on strike for around a week in 1994 after the last round of collective pay talks broke down.
Wage negotiations are also due to start in January at Enami's much larger Ventanas smelter and refinery which produces 240,000 tonnes of copper a year.
Ventanas was also hit by a walkout for 10 days two years ago after wage talks collapsed.
Chile's all-important copper industry has suffered a rash of strikes this year with stoppages at three pits including state copper company Codelco's Chuquicamata and Salvador mines.

Output at Chuquicamata, Codelco's largest division fell to 285,081 tonnes in the first six months of the year from 288,431 tonnes in the same period last year largely due to the 10 day strike at Chuquicamata in May.
